name: FedRAMP Rev 5 Moderate Baseline (NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5)
description: FedRAMP Moderate overlay for agents operating in or supporting federal cloud environments. Packages evidence for the six active AKSI evaluators with NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 control references aligned to the FedRAMP Moderate impact baseline, suitable for cloud service providers (CSPs) seeking or maintaining a FedRAMP authorization to operate (ATO).

evidence_requirements: PIV/CAC or equivalent phishing-resistant MFA is enforced for all privileged and remote access to federal systems and cloud service components
Identity provider meets FedRAMP-approved identity assurance requirements; access reviews are completed on a recurring basis aligned to the continuous monitoring (ConMon) program
Account lifecycle records demonstrate timely deprovisioning of separated employees, contractors, and service principals accessing FedRAMP-authorized environments
PR-01.framework_reference: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AC-2, AC-3, IA-2, IA-2(1), IA-2(2), IA-5, IA-8; FedRAMP Moderate Baseline AC-2, IA-2, IA-5

evidence_requirements: Separation of duties and least-privilege access controls are documented and enforced across FedRAMP authorization boundary functions and privileged administrative roles
Privileged access authorizations are time-bounded where feasible and reviewed on a cadence consistent with the FedRAMP Moderate ConMon program
Remote access restrictions enforce session encryption, source IP controls, and just-in-time approval workflows before privileged functions are invoked
PR-02.framework_reference: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AC-5, AC-6, AC-6(1), AC-14, AC-17, AC-17(2); FedRAMP Moderate Baseline AC-5, AC-6, AC-17

evidence_requirements: Baseline configuration documentation for all federal cloud components is current, version-controlled, and reviewed against USGCB or DISA STIG benchmarks where applicable
Change control board (CCB) or equivalent approval is documented for all configuration changes within the FedRAMP authorization boundary, including prompt, model, and tooling changes
Flaw remediation records show high and critical vulnerabilities are patched or mitigated within FedRAMP-required timeframes (high: 30 days, critical: immediate)
PR-03.framework_reference: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 CM-2, CM-3, CM-6, CM-7, CM-7(1), SI-2; FedRAMP Moderate Baseline CM-2, CM-3, CM-6, CM-7

evidence_requirements: FIPS 140-2/140-3 validated cryptographic modules protect federal data in transit and at rest; compensating controls are documented and accepted by the authorizing official when FIPS modules are unavailable
All data transmitted through or stored in FedRAMP-authorized components is protected by TLS 1.2+ or equivalent; downgrade attacks are mitigated at network boundaries
Media sanitization and disposal records demonstrate federal data is purged per NIST SP 800-88 Rev 1 guidelines before component decommission or reassignment
PR-04.framework_reference: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 SC-8, SC-8(1), SC-13, SC-28, SC-28(1), MP-2, MP-6; FedRAMP Moderate Baseline SC-8, SC-13, SC-28, MP-2

evidence_requirements: Audit event types are configured per the FedRAMP Moderate baseline audit requirements; log collection and alerting feeds into the agency or CSP continuous monitoring platform
Audit log integrity is verified through cryptographic signing or write-once storage; unauthorized modification or deletion generates automated alerts to the security operations team
Log review procedures confirm that anomalous events, failed access attempts, and privilege escalations are investigated and documented within FedRAMP ConMon reporting cycles
PR-05.framework_reference: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AU-2, AU-3, AU-3(1), AU-6, AU-9, AU-9(4), AU-12; FedRAMP Moderate Baseline AU-2, AU-3, AU-6, AU-9, AU-12

evidence_requirements: US-CERT notification path is documented and tested; significant cybersecurity incidents are reported within 1 hour of detection per FISMA and OMB M-20-04 requirements

Incident response plan is versioned, approved by the authorizing official, and reviewed annually or after significant incidents; roles and escalation procedures for federal system events are exercised
Continuous monitoring (ConMon) status demonstrates active vulnerability scanning, configuration drift detection, and security event aggregation across all FedRAMP authorization boundary components
DE-01.framework_reference: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 IR-4, IR-5, IR-6, IR-6(1), IR-8, SI-4, SI-4(2), SI-4(4); FedRAMP Moderate Baseline IR-4, IR-5, IR-6, IR-8, SI-4

reporting_obligations.assessment_type: FedRAMP Moderate authorization evidence package aligned to NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 control families for the six active AKSI evaluators. Supports annual assessment (3PAO) and continuous monitoring (ConMon) deliverables.
reporting_obligations.reporting_entity: Cloud service provider (CSP) security team, agency authorizing official (AO), and FedRAMP PMO as required by the authorization agreement and FISMA reporting obligations.

human_oversight_mandates.description: FedRAMP Moderate does not impose a per-AI-action human-in-the-loop mandate, but organizations must retain accountable human oversight over change control board approvals, incident response escalation, continuous monitoring findings, and annual 3PAO assessment activities.

notes: FedRAMP Rev 5 Moderate aligns cloud service providers to the NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 Moderate impact baseline for federal authorization. This overlay focuses on evidencing the six currently enforced AKSI evaluator controls with FedRAMP-specific evidence fields (PIV/CAC, FIPS 140, ConMon, US-CERT) while preserving a full 26-control framework mapping so federal cloud deployments can demonstrate authorization readiness without changing resolver logic. Evidence field names are non-overlapping with the CMMC-L2 overlay to support simultaneous activation when both overlays are triggered.
